title: Command Injection and Dynamic Code Execution Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: Shell command built from dynamic input
rules.description: os.system() or os.popen() receives a command string assembled with an f-string, '+' concatenation, '%' formatting, str.format() or string.Template. The string is handed to the system shell, so any interpolated value can append extra commands with shell metacharacters such as ;, |, && or $(...).

rules.name: subprocess call with shell=True and dynamic command
rules.description: subprocess.run(), Popen(), call(), check_output() or check_call() is invoked with shell=True and a dynamically built command string. shell=True routes the command through /bin/sh -c, so interpolated values are parsed as shell syntax instead of being passed as literal arguments.

rules.name: Dynamic eval() or exec() execution
rules.description: eval() or exec() is called with a value that is not a literal. When the argument is derived from request data, configuration or a database value, an attacker who can influence it achieves arbitrary Python code execution in the auditor process.
rules.remediation_example: value = ast.literal_eval(payload)  # or a strict allow-list mapping
